article.name: Cognis
article.summary: Cognis is a cloud-native agent controller that delegates durable memory to Mnemory. Its memory contribution is policy-controlled recall and write orchestration, an authenticated provider adapter, built-in memory tools, and a durable queue with optional event-bound trusted evidence. This source review does not assess Mnemory's internal memory implementation and includes no runtime measurements.

who_what.text: The curated catalog lists ordinal 137 as Cognis, slug cognis, with explicit locator https://github.com/fpytloun/cognis. The pinned Atlas entry is retained for roster attribution only, not as assessment evidence.

The official GitHub repository API identifies fpytloun/cognis as a public repository with main as its default branch; the official main ref and shallow checkout both report 7f1d5aee813d4a9e6a67d4703e45ccb90ab0eb80.
Cognis describes itself as a cloud-native Agent OS/controller for self-hosted agents. It owns orchestration and delegates persistent memory and recall to the companion Mnemory service.

architecture.text: Cognis resolves backend options into a frozen per-turn policy controlling bootstrap context, automatic recall, automatic remembering, and explicit tool availability. Mnemory offers full-auto, proactive, and on-demand modes; a policy fingerprint hashes configuration and instruction identity.

Mnemory remains the persistent memory system. Cognis implements the authenticated HTTP adapter and built-in memory tools, while the controller's relational database stores queued remember work. Production queue rows reference durable events and identities instead of embedding conversation text.

Cognis models optional trusted ingestion as a strict signed event envelope bound to source event content and user/owner/session/conversation/turn identity. Its lifecycle records describe admission and delivery outcomes, not memory truth or answer support.

behavior.text: Write: when policy enables auto-remember, the agent loop enqueues eligible user/assistant turn event references. The queue later reads source events and dispatches to Mnemory; the optional trusted evidence route binds an authenticated user event to its canonical hash and requires an enabled configuration and eligible owner allowlist.

Update and delete: built-in tools call Mnemory for add, batch add, update, delete, list, and artifact operations. The provider uses conditional If-Match revisions where alias-mediated mutations supply one; bootstrap identity replacement removes labeled old entries and carefully limits ambiguous legacy cleanup. The external service owns actual mutation semantics.

Retrieval: context preparation can issue a bounded, session-scoped search-mode recall when the policy enables it. Explicit memory_search, memory_find, and memory_ask tools provide semantic search, multi-angle query generation, and synthesized answers respectively; find/ask incur additional LLM calls. Cognis does not define the external ranking algorithm.

Scope isolation: provider calls require a user identity in a scoped runtime context and sign a JWT with that subject, adding agent and owner headers when available. Recall includes a Mnemory session ID and labels. Managed external channels disable ambient automatic recall and remember; mutations are denied and searches need an explicit safety allowance.

Provenance: ordinary queue entries use durable Intaris event references. Trusted evidence entries add event hashes, identities, admission markers, and typed delivery outcomes. This is source-event lineage, not a Cognis-owned memory record provenance model or claim-level citation feature.

Efficiency and observability: provider calls use retries and circuit-breaker handling; ordinary remember treats transport failure as outcome-unknown to avoid unsafe replay. Queue depth/retry/drop/success/replay and trusted evidence outcome/age metrics are defined; the operations guide documents provider health and queue depth/age reporting.

Known operational caveats include external Mnemory availability, separate ordinary and trusted write semantics, terminal trusted rejections that do not mean ingestion succeeded, and no automatic historical reconciliation through ordinary auto-remember.

metrics.evidence: The controller integrates recall and degraded-context handling, but no answerable/unanswerable gold workload was executed.
Update and replacement routes are wired; no correction probes or stale-value rate were measured.
Cognis forwards deletion to Mnemory; no residual-store or post-delete retrieval check was performed.
Identity binding and managed-channel restrictions are visible in source; no cross-user or cross-agent workload was executed.
Trusted writes bind to an input event, but no stored-memory or answer-level evidence audit was performed.
Timing and health instruments are defined; no latency distribution was collected.
No timed write-then-recall workload was run.
No memory-operation token or provider-cost accounting was performed.
Cognis queue storage is distinct from Mnemory's corpus; no corpus-size measurement was collected.

limits.text: This source review covers selected README, policy/backend, provider, context, memory tools, queue, evidence, managed-channel and operations files. It does not cover every API route, deployment configuration or failure path.

Mnemory implementation is outside the reviewed repository. Its retrieval algorithm, memory schema, correction/deletion guarantees, internal scope enforcement, retention and stored-record provenance remain unknown here.

No Cognis runtime, tests or benchmarks were run. Recall quality, abstention, correction, deletion completeness, scope isolation, latency, write-to-recall delay, cost and storage efficiency remain unmeasured.
Trusted evidence status and policy fingerprints establish request/admission lifecycle metadata, not that a saved memory is true or that a generated answer cites supporting evidence.
